More than 20 field officers from YAGASU are responsible for the different districts of the project areas ranging from east to west of the northern coast of Sumatra.
Generally, they are part of the communities and are well acquainted with the specific conditions within the different planting areas.
The forest inventory and monitoring surveys are conducted by them in the field (as part of the carbon survey teams).

And planting around 16,500,900 trees.
The seedlings come from the nursery carried out in the different villages involved in the project, where community groups are trained in good silvicultural practices to grow up the seedlings that will be used in the plantations.
A total amount of 18,150,991 seedlings have been grew up in 100 different villages.

Based on this characteristic, during mangrove planting, the project asked women to participate in establishing mangrove seedling, planting and managing trees, as well as students in elementary school, senior and junior high school, which are also involved in the planting activity.

 Planting (site preparation, planting, etc.): this activity was performed manually by local communities and with the support of Yagasu based on the technical guide for mangrove reforestation developed by the project with the advice of mangrove experts.
Most of the afforestation activities in YAGASU are in abandoned fish ponds and some on coastal/river mudflats.

 Planting (site preparation, planting, etc.): this activity was performed manually by local communities and with the support of Yagasu based on the technical guide for mangrove reforestation developed by the project with the advice of mangrove experts.
Most of the afforestation activities in YAGASU are in abandoned fish ponds and some on coastal/river mudflats.

Wildlife and its habitat threats identified in this Yagasu study were some activities including the felling of mangrove trees (in the Sei Meran area, registration is done to supply the raw material to make coal); and transfer of functions from mangrove forests to oil palm plantations (in Sei Meran) and aquaculture (in Beras Basarh, Sei Meran and Pulau Panjang).

The project region has up to 456,896 potential hectares for plantation and mangrove restoration and protection.
The grouped project has started with the implementation of the first project activity instance, which has been implemented as described in the PD.
In the first verification of the project Yagasu included 4,999.98 ha of degraded mangrove.
It is important to mention that, regarding the spatial data provided in shapefile format, in the first verification the area included was 5,068.69.
